title: Prehospital Suspicion of Fracture Following Ankle Trauma: A Retrospective Analysis of the Interface Between Emergency Medical Services and the Emergency Department
summary: Ankle injuries are a common reason for treatment by emergency medical services and in emergency departments. Before arrival at the hospital, emergency medical personnel have to assess whether a bone fracture may be present. The aim of this study is to investigate how well the assessment made by emergency medical services corresponds with the diagnosis subsequently established in the hospital. In addition, the study examines whether certain examination findings that can help determine the need for an X-ray can be assessed from the existing documentation. Only existing treatment data from adult patients are analyzed. No additional examinations, interviews or treatments are performed.
conditions: Acute ankle trauma with suspected fracture

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of adult patients (≥18 years) with acute ankle trauma who received prehospital emergency medical care and were subsequently presented to the emergency department. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adult patients (≥ 18 years) who presented to the emergency department of Siloah St. Trudpert Klinikum Pforzheim within the defined study period due to ankle trauma and who received prehospital emergency medical care. Cases are registered regardless of the completeness of prehospital and clinical diagnostic assessment. Cases with complete prehospital and clinical diagnostic assessment, including radiological findings, form the main analysis population.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients under 18 years of age; traumatic brain injury or relevant impairment of consciousness; polytrauma/severe injury in which assessment of an ankle fracture is of secondary importance in the prehospital setting; acute alcohol or other intoxication; neurological disorders with relevant sensory impairment, e.g. diabetic polyneuropathy; fractures of the proximal lower leg or tibial/fibular shaft (ICD-10-GM S82.1, S82.2).
